newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks hit 20th record close of year.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks hit 20th record close of year.

text.p: Toronto's stock market posted its 20th record close of the year on Thursday amid soaring gold issues as bullion prices bounced back from recent lows.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index added 18.31 points to close at 6592.92, inching above its old record of 6588.04 on July 3. But the index failed to break its all-time high of 6615.35 set the same day.
Gold bullion prices, which have danced recently around 12-year lows, rebounded on Thursday by $1.90 to $320.80 on Comex, buoying Toronto's influential golds.
"The volatility isn't over," said Fred Ketchen, ScotiaMcLeod's director of trading. "But this market reacts very positively every time it turns around."
Toronto's gold group, which makes up 8.4 percent of the 300 Index, jumped 2.9 percent and led 10 of the 14 sub-indexes higher. It was followed by media, consumer products and transportation.

Slipping oil and gas issues weighed down the 300 index after Renaissance Energy Ltd., one of Canada's top energy firms, reduced its forecast for 1997 oil production. Shocked investors sold off other energy companies after questioning their ability to meet production targets.
The other three falling sectors were base metals, banks and real estate.
Volume totaled 92 million shares worth C$1.4 billion ($1 billion). Rising issues outnumbered decliners 520 to 417, while 307 closed steady.
Renaissance dropped 3.20 to 36.10 in turnover of nearly 1.9 million shares and Talisman Energy Inc. slipped 0.60 to 43.60 in moderate trading.

Shares in Alcan Aluminium Ltd., the world's second largest aluminum producer, dropped 0.40 to 47.95. Alcan said second-quarter earnings rose to $116 million or $0.50 a share from a year ago $112 million or $0.47 a share.

Northern Telecom Ltd. jumped 1.85 to 134.60 in moderate trading. Canada's largest telecommunications equipment maker unveiled one of its largest contracts ever at $300 million after a group headed by Atlanta-based BellSouth Corp. contracted it to provide a digital cellular telephone network in Sao Paulo, Brazil.
